find_jobs:
{"description":"Marketplace job postings: search them by keywords and filters, get one by id, or get the jobs recommended for the freelancer's own profile (smart_search).

Actions:
- search: Search for jobs matching filters. Params: query (string — broad match across the WHOLE posting, title and description, with semantic expansion, so many results will not name the term at all; prefer title when the user asks for a specific kind of work), title (string — match the JOB TITLE only. This is how to cut noise when the user names a role ("React developer", "bookkeeper"): every returned job carries the words in its title. Terms are ANDed, so each word must appear in the title — use 1-3 key words and put everything else in the other filters, since a long title matches nothing. Case-insensitive and stemmed ("bookkeeper" matches "Bookkeeping"), whole words only ("Reac" matches nothing). Cannot be combined with query, which lets non-matching jobs back in, nor with sort=relevance, which drops the filter entirely — both are refused rather than silently ignored. An unmatched title returns no jobs, which is a real answer, not an error), job_type (fixed/hourly), experience_level (entry_level/intermediate/expert), budget_min (number), budget_max (number) (FIXED-PRICE project budget; each must be greater than 0; budget_min cannot exceed budget_max; omit a bound to leave it open. This does NOT filter hourly jobs — for an hourly rate use rate_min/rate_max), skills (array of string — filter to jobs carrying these Upwork skills, at most 5, ANDed: a job must carry every one, and nothing is dropped to find a match. Two unrelated skills routinely return nothing, which is a real answer — for a looser search put the same words in query, which matches the whole posting with semantic expansion. Names are matched exactly against the Upwork skill list; a name that does not match is reported and NOT applied, never guessed at. Relay filters_ignored when present so the user knows which skills were used), category (string — scope to a top-level category, by name ("Web, Mobile & Software Dev") or ontology id. An unknown name is rejected with the valid list rather than ignored), subcategory (string — same, one level down), rate_min (number), rate_max (number) (Hourly overlap: rate_min=X matches posted max >= X; rate_max=Y matches posted min <= Y — not strict bounds. Budget is A–B/hr, A+/hr, or up to B/hr. True floor: keep min>=X, drop up-to and no-range. True ceiling: keep max<=Y, drop A+/hr and no-range. Values >0, min <= max; pair with job_type=hourly), workload (full_time/part_time/as_needed), duration (less_than_1_month/1_to_3_months/3_to_6_months/more_than_6_months — expected project length; this is distinct from workload, which is hours per week. It constrains HOURLY jobs only: fixed-price jobs are returned regardless of their duration, so combine it with job_type=hourly when the user asks for work of a given length), verified_payment_only (boolean — only jobs from clients with a verified payment method), proposals_min (number), proposals_max (number) (RANGE over proposals already submitted — there is no exactly-N filter; e.g. proposals_max=5 for jobs with fewer than 5 proposals), client_hires_min (number), client_hires_max (number) (filter by the client's past hire count; e.g. client_hires_min=0, client_hires_max=0 for clients with no hires, or client_hires_min=10 for 10+). Range bounds must be >= 0 and min cannot exceed max; omit a bound to leave it open. Each job carries a client block: total_spent (lifetime spend), total_reviews, rating, total_posted_jobs (how many jobs this client has ever posted — that is NOT a hire count and must never be reported as one), verification_status and country. It does NOT carry a hire count — client_hires_min/max filter on a number these rows cannot show, so never report one from a search result; use get on a job for client_record, which has the hires alongside the spend. rating there is the score FREELANCERS gave that client (client_rating_basis in the response says so) — treat a low rating as a warning about the client, not as the client being unsuccessful. sort (recency/relevance/client_total_charge/client_rating — omit for newest-first, except when query is set without title, skills, category or subcategory, where the default is relevance. relevance is REFUSED alongside title, skills, category or subcategory, because upstream drops those filters and returns a page that was never narrowed; the other three keep every filter), previous_clients_only (boolean — only jobs from clients you have worked with before), timezone (string — filter by the client's timezone, as an IANA name like America/New_York), location (string — filter by the client's location, as a country or region name like "United States" or "Europe"). These two take a fixed vocabulary: a value outside it returns an empty page rather than an error, so when a search using either comes back with no jobs, READ filters_rejected — it names the value that was rejected and gives the accepted spelling to retry with. limit (integer, 1–10, default 10), include_full_details (boolean, default false — when true, each job also includes its full untruncated description from this SAME search response, avoiding one get call per result. This can make the response large; leave it false when summaries are enough), cursor (string — omit for the first page; to fetch the next page, repeat the SAME filters with cursor set to the endCursor from the previous response's pageInfo, and only when pageInfo.hasNextPage is true). A client's preferred qualifications are NOT in search results — use get on a specific job to see them. Proposal visibility follows the account plan: Freelancer Plus results include exact proposal_count, while Basic and other accounts include only proposals_tier (Fewer than 5, 5 to 10, 10 to 15, 15 to 20, 20 to 50, or 50+). If the plan cannot be verified, the safer tier is returned. Each result also includes applied (true when THIS freelancer already applied — never recommend applying again, and say so instead), featured (true when Upwork promotes the posting in the Find Work list — say "featured", never "premium"), and, when the freelancer has worked with the client before, previous_client with that client's company_name and last_contract_title. Signed-in results carry job_activity (get's jobActivity as total_hired, …): hiring counts, not a closed flag; absent: see job_activity_note. This action has NO DATE FILTER: the signed-in job search takes no date field at all, so do NOT tell the user results were narrowed to a time window here. For a REAL date filter use find_jobs action=smart_search with mode=most_recent, which is backed by the recommendation feed and does honour dates: days_posted for "posted today/this week", or from_date/to_date for an explicit range. Those results are personalized to the freelancer rather than the whole marketplace. On this action, the best available approximation is sort=recency plus each result's created_date/published_date for client-side narrowing. Each result also has url (job link).
- get: Get full details of a job posting including client company info, work history, connects, and the client's preferred qualifications (preferred_qualifications: e.g. contractor_type, job success score, English level, earnings, languages, tests) and location (preferred_locations; your_location = region match; regions never block applying); surface both. Freelancer responses include connects_cost (required to apply), connects_balance, can_apply, applied and a ready-to-use url. Missing Connects data carries connects_cost_unavailable plus a reason/note; never infer zero. applied means a proposal exists; can_apply is then false. Never recommend applying again. client_record is the client's hiring record — hires, active contracts, total spend, feedback score and count, hours, jobs posted, hire rate (hire_rate_percent) and open jobs; surface it when the user is judging whether the client is worth applying to. It is read live for this job, so where a search row's client block (total_posted_jobs, total_spent, rating, total_reviews) differs, client_record is the current figure. When the response carries bid_stats_basis, the bid amounts under activityStat.applicationsBidStats have no unit attached. activityStat.jobActivity carries this posting's hiring funnel: invitesSent, totalInvitedToInterview, totalHired and totalOffered. Read them to judge whether the posting is still live and how far along hiring already is — a job that has hired or made offers is a weaker bet than an untouched one. These are counts for THIS posting, not the client's lifetime record; that is client_record. proposals_tier_unavailable and unanswered_invites_unavailable mark missing data, never zero. Use search for proposal competition data, subject to its account-plan rules. client_work_history holds the client's 5 latest open and 5 latest closed contracts, in separate open/closed lists (its selection field says so), so never derive totals or a count of open jobs from it — client_record has the totals. client_open_jobs lists up to 5 of the client's OTHER open jobs visible to freelancers (id, title, job_type, url); it is a sample, never a count. client_record.open_jobs counts ALL open jobs, including private ones and this one, so never present the difference as more jobs the user could browse. client_feedback holds up to 5 of the latest reviews freelancers wrote about this client; a comment often names the client contact or the project — use it to personalize a proposal, never inferring a name no comment gives. Params: id or job_id (required string): numeric id, ~02… ciphertext, or Upwork job URL (accepted directly). Serves clients and freelancers. The 403 denial this action can return is usually Upwork's per-account browse throttle (sometimes a private posting): after several denials in a row without a successful get in between, the server cooldowns job-detail opens for about a minute (error_code JOB_BROWSE_COOLDOWN) — stop opening jobs and work from search results until it clears.
- smart_search: Personalized job recommendations for the signed-in freelancer, from Upwork's own recommender — the same feeds behind the Find Work page. Prefer this over action=search whenever the user wants work for themselves ("find me jobs", "what should I apply to"); use action=search when they supply their own search terms. Do NOT pass skills from the profile: the recommender already knows the freelancer's profile, history and what they have applied to, and takes no query. Each result includes a ready-to-use url. TWO FEEDS. mode=best_match (the DEFAULT) ranks by fit. mode=most_recent returns the newest postings matched to this freelancer, newest first — not the whole marketplace. Whenever you return best_match results, TELL THE USER that Most Recent is also available and offer it; switch to mode=most_recent as soon as they ask for the newest, latest or just-posted work. The response repeats this in mode_note — relay it. Params: mode (best_match/most_recent), skills (array of string, at most 5 — names are matched exactly against the Upwork skill list; a name that does not match is reported and NOT applied, never guessed at. The feed has no skills filter, so these are matched against the recommended jobs after they come back, NOT sent to Upwork — so a short page does not mean little work exists. Relay filters_ignored when present), days_posted (integer >= 1 — only jobs posted in the last N days; days_posted=1 means "posted today"), from_date / to_date (YYYY-MM-DD, or RFC3339 for finer granularity — an explicit range instead of a rolling window; to_date is inclusive of the whole day, and defaults to now when only from_date is given. Cannot be combined with days_posted). These three are the ONLY working date filters in find_jobs, and they apply to mode=most_recent — the best_match recommender picks its own set and ignores the window, so pair any date request with mode=most_recent. action=search cannot filter by date at all. These filters take the same values and rules as on action=search: job_type, experience_level, budget_min/budget_max (FIXED-PRICE only), rate_min/rate_max (HOURLY overlap, not strict; one-sided/no-range: see search), category, subcategory, workload, duration (HOURLY jobs only), verified_payment_only, proposals_min/proposals_max, client_hires_min/client_hires_max, previous_clients_only, timezone, location. limit (integer, 1–10, default 10), cursor (string, optional — omit for the first page; to fetch the next page repeat the SAME filters and the SAME mode with cursor set to the next_cursor from the previous response, only when hasMore is true). Each result also carries connect_price (what applying costs), job_activity (as on search) and applied — never recommend applying to a job where applied is true.

manage_proposals:
{"description":"Submit, edit, or withdraw freelancer proposals. Submitting can include a Connects boost bid for a top slot on the client's list. Also accept or decline client job invitations. For client offers, use respond_to_offer. Freelancers cannot send the first message on a proposal — see PROPOSAL MESSAGING.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
Returns a preview — call confirm_preview only after explicit user approval.

Actions:
- create: Prepare a proposal draft for a marketplace job. EXISTING INVITE/PROPOSAL CHECK — MANDATORY, NEVER SKIP: before preparing a create draft you MUST call list_freelancer_proposals action=invitations to check whether the freelancer already has an invitation for this job, and action=list to check for an existing (pending, active, or declined) proposal. If an invitation exists, do NOT use create — use accept_invitation instead. Upwork rejects create when either exists (VJ-JA-10). Returns a preview (confirm_preview type='proposal') — the proposal is NOT submitted yet. Preview includes connects_cost (the connects REQUIRED to apply — the job's price, NOT the freelancer's balance), connects_balance (the freelancer's available connects), whether the freelancer can apply, and bid stats (avg/min/max rates from other proposals). bid_stats is a Freelancer Plus feature: when the account is not entitled it is replaced by bid_stats_available:false plus bid_stats_note — relay that note's framing and never estimate the amounts yourself. preview.plan is the account's plan name; mention it only when it explains a limitation the user ran into. Preview also includes a 'boost' block — boosting is a connects BID (not a flat fee) for a top slot on the client's list; Upwork charges it only if you finish in the paid slots (see boost.note for this job's actual count) or the client engages the proposal before the auction closes. If boost.available is false, do NOT offer boosting at all — it is unavailable (e.g. you do not meet the client's preferred qualifications; see boost.reason). Otherwise: boost.current_top_bids are the ACTUAL competing bids on this job (highest first; empty if no one has boosted) — present those, not any invented numbers. If boost.current_top_bids_available is false the bids could not be fetched — say the current bids are unknown; do NOT say no one has boosted. Offer boosting unless boost.recommendation is 'skip' (e.g. the client already hired). boost.recommended_connects is the smallest bid that secures a top slot (often just 1 connect when few or none have boosted) — note it and let the user pick any amount at or above it. A bid BELOW it is refused rather than submitted: a bid that cannot take a paid slot ties up the user's connects for nothing. Never exceed boost.max_boost_connects — the bid is spent from the same balance the proposal itself costs, so it is your_balance minus connects_cost, not your_balance; apply ONLY the amount the user approves (pass it to create as boost_connects — a whole number of connects, at least 1). A submitted bid cannot be changed; verify it with list_freelancer_proposals action=get, which reports terms.connectsBid as Upwork stored it. Confirmation re-reads the bids; if the approved bid no longer takes a paid slot, the proposal is NOT submitted and you get the bids to beat so the user can approve a new amount. If the preview contains unmet_preferred_qualifications, tell the user which of the client's preferred qualifications their proposal does not meet. For additional_preferences (e.g. regions), follow its note. Neither blocks submission. Present the full preview to the user and ask for confirmation. ALWAYS state connects_cost (the Connects this application will spend) and connects_balance explicitly when you present the preview — never omit the Connects cost. Offer to strengthen the proposal by attaching highlights: ASK the user whether they want any, call get_profile action=list_highlights, show the titles, and pass ONLY the ids the user chose as certificate_ids / portfolio_project_ids / work_history_ids (past Upwork jobs — the ones with client feedback). FILE ATTACHMENTS — MANDATORY, NEVER SKIP: before submitting, you MUST ask the user whether they want to attach any files to the proposal (e.g. a resume/CV, work samples, a brief). Never silently skip this question, even though the field is optional. If they say yes, call start_attachment_upload with context='proposals' FIRST, wait for the upload to complete, and pass the returned file_uid values as the attachments param. Submitted proposals show as Pending in list_freelancer_proposals. Params: job_reference (string, required — the numeric jobs[].id from find_jobs action=search, NOT the ~02… ciphertext field), cover_letter (string, required unless ai_interview — max 5000 characters; keep it concise, and if the user's text is longer ask them to shorten it rather than sending it truncated), application_method (cover_letter | ai_interview, when asked), charged_amount (number, required — bid amount; not a string). scheduled_rate_increase ({percent, frequency_months}, optional — a scheduled increase of the hourly rate the freelancer proposes: percent 1 to 99.9 with at most one decimal place, frequency_months 3, 6, 12. Include it only when the user asks for one; omit it for no raise. Upwork refuses it on jobs from Enterprise clients), answers (array of {question, answer}, optional — required only when the job has screening_questions, surfaced in the create preview: answer each and pass them here so they submit with the proposal). boost_connects (integer, optional — whole number of connects BID to boost the proposal's rank; at least boost.recommended_connects, never more than boost.max_boost_connects (your_balance less the proposal's own connects_cost). A bid that would not take one of the job's paid slots is REFUSED, not submitted). team_org_id (string, optional — only for an agency with more than one team: the team the proposal is submitted under. Omit it; if the agency has several teams the error names them, and the user picks one). attachments (array of strings, optional — file_uid values from start_attachment_upload with context='proposals'). certificate_ids, portfolio_project_ids, work_history_ids (optional arrays of ids from get_profile list_highlights). Org comes from org_uid on execute_tool (maps to teamOrgId).
  Prior context: before creating, look up recent/relevant prior items when available: call list_freelancer_proposals action=list/get for prior proposals; start with recent Accepted proposals and, for strongest templates, also check Offered/Hired examples; use find_jobs or the target job details for the current job. Use prior items to infer cover letter tone, structure, relevant experience, bid patterns, and job-specific requirements, but do not invent required write params. COVER LETTER — make it authentic and specific, never generic or fake-sounding, and ground every claim in the freelancer's REAL history (get_profile for work history and profile aggregates, list_freelancer_proposals for past Accepted/Hired proposals, and get_profile action=list_highlights for projects and certificates): (1) Weave in the most RELEVANT past jobs — what was delivered and the outcome. If none are directly relevant, still cite strong past jobs as evidence of the freelancer's quality and reliability. (2) Reference concrete, REAL signals of client satisfaction (feedback score, repeat clients, Top Rated status) and the quality of past deliverables — never invent praise, metrics, or clients. (3) Include the freelancer's relevant PROJECTS (portfolio work done outside Upwork jobs) and CERTIFICATIONS: mention them in the letter AND suggest attaching them via portfolio_project_ids / certificate_ids. (4) LANGUAGE: if the job requires a language other than English, provide the SAME cover letter in that language as well (English plus the required language) so the client can read it in their own language. (5) PERSONALIZE: before drafting, read client_feedback from find_jobs action=get (or user.name on the invitation). When a review names the client contact or the project, open by addressing the contact by name and referencing that project. Never guess or infer a name that no review or invitation states. Keep it human, specific, and honest — no boilerplate.
- accept_invitation: Accept a client invitation and submit a proposal (confirm_preview type='proposal_accept_invitation'; accepting creates a client-visible proposal). Use this, not create, when a client invited the freelancer. Get the invitation_uid from list_freelancer_proposals action=invitations (the 'id' field). FILE ATTACHMENTS — MANDATORY, NEVER SKIP: ask about attachments before confirming, exactly as described for create; the COVER LETTER rules under create apply here too. Params: invitation_uid (string, required), cover_letter (string, optional — max 5000 characters), bid (number, optional — proposed rate/amount), boost_connects (integer, optional — as for create), scheduled_rate_increase ({percent, frequency_months}, optional — a scheduled increase of the hourly rate the freelancer proposes: percent 1 to 99.9 with at most one decimal place, frequency_months 3, 6, 12. Include it only when the user asks for one; omit it for no raise. Upwork refuses it on jobs from Enterprise clients), application_method (cover_letter | ai_interview, when asked), fixed-price terms (as for create, when asked), attachments (array of strings, optional — file_uid values from start_attachment_upload with context='proposals'). answers (array of {question, answer}, optional — required only when the invited job has screening questions: answer each and pass them here so they submit with the accepted proposal, exactly as with action=create). team_org_id (string, optional — as for create).
- start_ai_interview: Preview opening a job's AI interview room; confirm_preview returns the link. Each join spends an attempt. Params: job_reference.
- decline_invitation: Decline a client job invitation (confirm_preview type='proposal_decline_invitation'; declining notifies the client). Get the invitation_uid from list_freelancer_proposals action=invitations (the 'id' field). Params: invitation_uid (string, required), reason_id (string, optional — canned decline reason ID; required when message is provided), reason_other (string, optional — free-text reason), message (string, optional — message to the client; requires reason_id), block_client (boolean, optional — block the client after declining).
- withdraw: Withdraw a pending proposal (confirm_preview type='proposal_withdraw'). The proposal must be in a withdrawable state (e.g. Pending). Params: proposal_id (string, required — the proposal ID), reason_id (string, optional — a withdrawal reason by its id or label, e.g. 'Applied by mistake'; an unknown value is refused and the valid reasons are listed), other_reason (string, optional — free-text reason if not using a canned reason), message (string, optional — message to the client about the withdrawal). If the proposal was boosted, the preview carries boost_connects and a boost_warning — state both to the user before confirming, since withdrawing forfeits those Connects and blocks re-applying to this job.
- edit: Edit a submitted proposal (confirm_preview type='proposal_edit_terms'). Params: proposal_id and at least one field to change (see the schema). Omitted fields keep their current values. boost_connects adds a boost only to a proposal submitted WITHOUT one; the preview's boost block has the bounds. certificate_ids / portfolio_project_ids / work_history_ids come from get_profile list_highlights.
- send_proposal: Propose a contract directly to a client you are already in a conversation with (e.g. after they invited you or replied to your proposal). NOT binding — a contract only starts if the client accepts and funds it (confirm_preview type='contract_proposal'). The client is derived from the conversation, so you do NOT supply client IDs; the CLIENT must have opened the room. Params: room_id (string, required — the conversation/Dash room ID from get_messages), title (string, required — contract title), hourly_rate (string, required — e.g. '55.00'), currency (string, default USD), weekly_limit (number, optional — max weekly hours), description (string, optional).

get_messages:
{"description":"List rooms, find rooms by context, and read messages.

Actions:
- list_rooms: List your rooms, most-recently-active first. The count of rooms is not available, so never state a total. Page with cursor while hasMore is true. Params: unread_only (boolean, optional — only rooms with unread messages), room_type (ALL/GROUP/ONE_ON_ONE/INTERVIEW, default ALL), limit (integer, 1–100, default 10), cursor (string, optional — next_cursor from a prior list for the next page; alias: after). unread_only and room_type both carry a note in the response describing what the filtered list does and does not cover. Room cards carry last_message_from_self, and — when the last sender can be placed — last_message_side (client/freelancer) and awaiting_reply_from (you/them). awaiting_reply_from is ABSENT when the sender could not be placed, which in a shared room usually means a colleague of one of the two parties wrote last; read the thread with list_messages instead of assuming. Only unread_only/room_type lists, find_room and search_rooms carry latestStory.from_org_type (see list_messages).
- search_rooms: Find your own past conversations by free text — a participant's name (a first name is enough), a room name, or a topic. This is the way to locate an old thread with someone when you do not have its room_id: do NOT use find_freelancers for that, which searches the public marketplace rather than your own conversations. Results are room cards in the same shape list_rooms returns; pass a room's id to list_messages to read it. Params: query (string, required — the name or text to search for), limit (integer, 1–10, default 10), offset (number, optional — next_offset from a prior search for the next page; must be a multiple of limit). Cards carry the same turn signals list_rooms describes. A response with partial true is MISSING matches that failed to load — report it as incomplete and offer to retry, never as the full set of results.
- find_room: Find a room by context. Params: context_type (contract/offer/proposal/one_on_one, required), context_id (string, required), organization_id (string, required for one_on_one). A not-found is final until a conversation starts; do not retry the same context_id. For context_type=proposal: Freelancers cannot send the first message on a proposal — see PROPOSAL MESSAGING.
- list_messages: List messages in a room, NEWEST FIRST — the default page is the tail of the conversation, not the whole thread. Before summarising a thread or answering whether something was ever discussed, page back with cursor while hasMore is true; the message count is not available, so never state one. Params: room_id (string, required), limit (integer, 1–100, default 20), cursor (string, optional — next_cursor from a prior call for the next page of older messages; alias: after). message_count is present only once the whole thread has been read (hasMore false); while paging, the number of messages in the room is unknown. Each message carries from (author name), from_self, and — when known — from_side (client/freelancer: which side of the deal wrote it) and from_my_organization. To tell your own team from the other party in a shared room use from_side, NOT from_organization: that field is the org a message was posted under, which reflects how the sender was invited to the room rather than which side they are on, so reading it as a side indicator gives the wrong answer. from_self only means you wrote it, so a teammate's message is not from_self either. from_org_type is client or agency; when agency, present the sender as <from> on behalf of <from_organization>. A freelancer-side message without it can still come from an agency member (members often post from their personal account): the proposal's applicant_type (list_client_proposals action=list) is authoritative.
- get_message: Get a single message. Params: room_id (string, required), story_id (string, required). Carries from_org_type like list_messages.

list_freelancer_proposals:
{"description":"View your freelancer proposals and received invitations. Prior proposals make good drafting examples. Note: the status 'Accepted' means the proposal was submitted and validated (NOT that the client accepted you) — each result includes a status_label with the plain-English meaning. Start with recent submitted (Accepted) proposals; when looking for the strongest templates, also check Offered/Hired examples. list shows only Accepted by default: when a proposal the user asks about is not there, also check Offered, Hired, Declined and Withdrawn before saying it does not exist, and tell them which status it was under.

Actions:
- list: List your proposals with status (plus status_label), bid terms, created/modified dates, viewedByClient, and job id/title. Each proposal carries boosted (true/false) and, when boosted, terms.connectsBid — the Connects bid Upwork actually STORED. This is the figure to report and the way to verify a boost after submitting: it is read back from Upwork, not the number that was sent. If it differs from what the user asked for, tell them the stored value and that the bid cannot be changed through this tool. Params: status (string, default Accepted — which means 'submitted'; values: Accepted=submitted, Offered=offer received, Hired, Activated=invitation accepted, Pending=processing, Declined, Withdrawn, Archived), sort_field (CREATEDDATETIME/MODIFIEDDATETIME, default CREATEDDATETIME), sort_order (ASC/DESC, default DESC), limit (integer, 1–25, default 25), cursor (string, optional — pageInfo.endCursor from a prior list for the next page; alias: after).
- invitations: List invitations you received from clients. The 'id' field in each result is the invitation_uid needed for manage_proposals action=accept_invitation. Each result includes jobPosting (id + title); for full job details call find_jobs action=get with jobPosting.id. Params: status (string, default pending), job_posting_id (string, optional — only invitations for that job), include_client (boolean, default false — adds client_record and client_open_jobs as on find_jobs action=get: client_open_jobs is a sample, never a count; client_record.open_jobs counts all open jobs, including private ones and the invited job; one extra lookup per distinct job), sort_field (CREATED, default CREATED), sort_order (ASC/DESC, default DESC), limit (integer, 1–25, default 25), cursor (string, optional — pageInfo.endCursor from a prior list for the next page; alias: after).
- get: Full proposal details; viewedByClient = client opened it. Carries boosted and terms.connectsBid exactly as described for list (the STORED bid — report that value). Params: id or proposal_id (string, required — from list). The response may include insights: how many proposals the job has, how many the client opened, shortlisted or messaged, and what the competing applicants look like on average (earnings, completed jobs, years on Upwork, Job Success Score) plus their most common skills. Present them as the client's activity and the field so far, not as a verdict on the proposal. When insights_available is false, relay insights_note as written: never say the job has no other applicants, and never estimate the numbers yourself.
- get_room: Get the messaging room for a proposal. Params: proposal_id (string, required). Freelancers cannot send the first message on a proposal — see PROPOSAL MESSAGING.

get_profile:
{"description":"View your own profile, transaction history, and connects balance.

Actions:
- get: Your own profile; no params. Another freelancer's profile is find_freelancers get_profile. Job aggregates count completed contracts: totalFixedJobs and totalHourlyJobs are the component counts, and totalJobs is their reconciled sum. Your own profile also carries promotions: free-Connects tasks, an earn_connects nudge, and the Freelancer Plus offer (share its url exactly as returned).
- list_highlights: List what can be attached to a proposal as highlights: certificates (id, name), portfolio_projects (id, title) and work_history — past Upwork contracts with dates and client_feedback. When drafting a proposal, show them and pass only the ids the user chooses to manage_proposals create as certificate_ids / portfolio_project_ids / work_history_ids. No params.

- connects_balance: Get connects balance and recent usage history. Shows the current balance (connectsBalance, the spendable total = free + paid) and recent connects transactions with job titles. balance is the general Connects wallet; product_credits (when present) are ad credits spendable only on the named product and are NOT included in it — report them separately, never summed.
